observations.content: Used named function declarations (onMessage, onClose, onError) instead of anonymous arrow functions for WebSocket event listeners. This is required because removeListener needs a reference to the exact function that was added. Anonymous functions cannot be removed.

Tracked channel subscription handlers in a Map<string, handler> on each Client object so that channel EventEmitter listeners can be individually removed on disconnect, preventing the second source of the memory leak.

The memory leak had two sources: (1) WebSocket event listeners (message/close/error) not being removed on disconnect, and (2) channel EventEmitter listeners accumulating as clients subscribed to channels. Both needed cleanup in the disconnect handler.

When a client re-subscribes to the same channel, the old handler must be removed first to prevent duplicate listeners. The subscribe handler now checks for and removes existing handlers before adding new ones.

The test suite uses a lightweight MockWebSocket class (no real ws dependency needed) that tracks listeners in a Map<string, Set<Function>>. Tests validate cleanup across 100 connect/disconnect cycles to catch accumulation bugs.
This repo uses 'npx tsx' to run TypeScript tests directly. Test command: npm test → npx tsx src/__tests__/handler.test.ts. No test framework — uses a custom test/assert pattern.
